Cyndi Munson

Democratic candidate for Governor, Oklahoma · Open seat

Former state legislator (Oklahoma House Minority Leader)

Cyndi Munson is the Democratic nominee for governor of Oklahoma. She has served in the Oklahoma House of Representatives since 2015 and was the first Asian-American woman elected to the Oklahoma Legislature. Her House service ended after the 2026 legislative session, when she was Minority Leader. She won the Democratic nomination in 2026 and will face Republican Mike Mazzei and three independent candidates on November 3, 2026.

Where Munson stands

Taxes
Opposes across-the-board income tax cuts and argues they mostly benefit high earners and shrink state revenue. Supports targeted tax relief for working families.
Education
Supports more funding for public schools and higher teacher pay. Proposes repealing the state's private school tax credit, expanding Oklahoma's Promise, and providing free school meals.
State spending
Says she would move state money from private school voucher programs and corporate tax incentives into public schools, teacher pay, rural hospitals, and childcare.
Data centers
Says that on her first day in office she would sign an executive order pausing new data center construction. Supports more regulation of data centers.
Abortion
Supports a state question to repeal Oklahoma's abortion ban and protect abortion access in the state Constitution.
Health care / Medicaid
Pledges to protect Medicaid expansion. Opposes moving it out of the state constitution and into regular law.
Childcare
Supports keeping childcare subsidies and giving tax incentives to employers who help pay employees' childcare costs.
Wages and housing
Supports raising the minimum wage and offering incentives to build affordable housing.
Inola smelter incentives
Says she voted against a $250 million incentive package in 2025, citing concerns about land, water, and air contamination.
